answer:
Full jitter replaces the computed backoff delay with a uniform draw between zero and that delay, spreading retries that would otherwise share a deadline. Without it, clients that failed together retry together, so a synchronized wave arrives when the service is least able to absorb load. Randomizing each delay decorrelates arrivals; the book's retry-storm failure mode calls the unjittered case an immediate load spike. Jitter alone is insufficient: retry budgets, backpressure and timeouts also bound amplification. A synthetic A/B/C run reported amplification 1.004 and 0.41% timeouts for three attempts, exponential backoff and full jitter, versus 1.079 and 11.1% for two attempts with linear backoff; differing parameters mean this illustrates the combination, not jitter alone.

Recording is required because the policy is an input. V12 scenarios declare backoff and jitter, use a base seed with deterministic per-replication seeds, and run provenance stores model and scenario hashes plus the seed base; replay recomputes the result hash and fails on drift. If jitter is omitted, the scenario hash does not bind it; replay may draw under a different policy and metrics no longer match the recorded configuration. Confidence is high for mechanism and contracts; the run is synthetic, and replication does not validate assumed distributions.

evidence.claim: Full jitter replaces the computed backoff delay with a uniform draw between zero and that delay.
evidence.note: Observed: 'Full jitter replaces the delay with a uniform draw between zero and the computed delay.'

evidence.claim: Without jitter, many clients that failed at the same time retry at the same time, creating synchronized retry waves.
evidence.note: Observed: 'Jitter reduces synchronized retry waves: without it, many clients that failed at the same time retry at the same time.'

evidence.claim: Retry storm is a failure mode in which every client retries immediately, adding a load spike when the service is least able to handle it.
evidence.note: Observed: 'Every client retries immediately. The service sees a load spike just as it is least able to handle it.'

evidence.claim: In the synthetic A/B/C comparison, candidate B (three attempts, exponential backoff, full jitter) had retry amplification 1.004 and timeout rate 0.0041; candidate C (two attempts, linear backoff) had 1.079 and 0.111.
evidence.note: Observed: run-reported values. Inference: attempts, backoff shape and jitter differ together, so the comparison illustrates the combination rather than isolating jitter's effect.

evidence.claim: Jitter alone does not prevent overload; retry budget, backpressure, queue capacity and timeout limits must bound the system together.
evidence.note: Observed: the overview says retry budgets, backoff and jitter are needed, and backpressure, queue capacity and bulkhead decide explicit rejection or collapse. Inference: no single mechanism is sufficient.

evidence.claim: The scenario declares the jitter choice, and a model that uses jitter without recording it is not reproducible.
evidence.note: Observed: 'The scenario declares the choice. A model that uses jitter without recording it is not reproducible.'

evidence.claim: The scenario contract's configuration includes attempts and backoff, alongside the model, workload, uncertainty, replications and seed scheme.
evidence.note: Observed: required structure lists configuration with attempts and backoff, plus replications and seed.

evidence.claim: V12 uses a base seed and deterministic per-replication seed; the run record stores the base seed and replication count.
evidence.note: Observed: 'A seed is not a random number chosen to make a result look stable. It is part of the input contract.'

evidence.claim: Run provenance stores model and scenario hashes plus the seed base, and replay recomputes the result hash, failing on drift.
evidence.note: Observed: provenance includes 'model hash, scenario hash, seed base, replications'; 'Replay recomputes it and fails if the model, scenario or engine output has drifted.'

evidence.claim: Replication reduces sampling error but does not validate assumed input distributions.
evidence.note: Observed: 'more replications make the assumption more precise, not more true.'
